newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine court declines halt drug campaign mayor.
newsitem.headline: Philippine court declines halt drug campaign mayor.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court has declined to stop a controversial anti-drugs campaign by Manila Mayor Alfredo Lim, referring the case to a lower court, according to court documents released on Friday.
Human rights lawyers petitioned the court to stop Lim from ordering police to spray-paint the doors of suspected drug pushers, saying the campaign was unconstitutional.

"After deliberating on these petitions... the Court resolves to transfer these two cases to the Regional Trial Court of Pasig City for appropriate action," Clerk of Court Luzviminda Puno said in a one-page memorandum.
Puno did not give any explanation.
Lim's campaign sparked an uproar when police marked the houses of alleged drug pushers and addicts with signs such as "Beware, drug pusher's house", "Get out", and "Drug pusher lives here."

A group of human rights lawyers and the Integrated Bar of the Philippines said the campaign "degrades the dignity and integrity of those whose houses are spray-painted in that they immediately condemn said owners and occupants ... as drug pushers without the benefit of a public trial."
A resident of one of the more than 200 houses that have been painted said he was not a drug pusher and had been falsely accused.
